players.product: biosimulation, regulatory science, and AI-assisted drug-development software

quarterly_data.signal: Interim CFO Faiz Mohammed: the divestiture of the Regulatory and Medical Writing business closed on May 8; through the close that business contributed $19.2 million of revenue and $7.5 million of adjusted EBITDA, both reported in discontinued operations. CEO Jon Resnick: the divestiture was the first step in sharpening the strategy and rebalancing Certara; the divested business had a roughly 30% margin profile. The company is reorganized around two business units, Model Informed Discovery and Drug Development (MID3) and Accelerated Clinical Evidence (ACE).
quarterly_data.figure: divested business: $19.2 million revenue and $7.5 million adjusted EBITDA through the May 8 close; roughly 30% margin profile

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jon Resnick: in May Certara executed a reduction in force focused predominantly on overhead, impacting approximately 5% of its global employee base; combined with other operational-excellence steps it is expected to deliver run-rate savings of approximately $13 million, addressing stranded costs from the divestiture and funding AI and product investment. In Q&A he confirmed the $13 million is incremental to the formerly identified savings plan. Interim CFO Faiz Mohammed: reorganization costs rose $2.2 million year over year in Q2.
quarterly_data.figure: ~5% of global employees; ~$13 million run-rate savings; reorganization costs +$2.2 million

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 revenue grew 1% year over year on a reported basis: software revenue rose 4%, driven by Simcyp, Phoenix and Pinnacle 21, while services revenue fell 3% to $44.5 million. Software now represents 53% of the business versus 40% two years ago. Trailing 12-month bookings were $405.4 million (+3%) and trailing 12-month software bookings $196.4 million (+8%); normalizing for the Chemaxon acquisition, trailing 12-month bookings grew 7% exiting the first half, up from 0.8% exiting 2025. CEO: absolute renewal rates were up in the quarter, slightly ahead of expectation, and there is no particular net-retention issue.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue +1%; software +4%; services $44.5 million (-3%); software 53% of business (40% two years ago); TTM bookings $405.4 million (+3%); TTM software bookings $196.4 million (+8%)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 total bookings were $98.3 million (+1%). Services bookings were $47.6 million, down 6%, a services book-to-bill of 1.07, impacted in part by the carve-out of the regulatory and medical writing business; trailing 12-month services bookings were $209 million (-1%). CEO Jon Resnick: the pipeline grew 27% year on year exiting the quarter, which management anticipates translating into revenue growth in the back half of 2026; replacing the generalist sales model deployed two years ago with specialist, PhD-led engagement is driving the biggest spike in pipeline and a higher percentage of scientific services in it.
quarterly_data.figure: total bookings $98.3 million (+1%); services bookings $47.6 million (-6%); book-to-bill 1.07; TTM services bookings $209 million (-1%); pipeline +27%

quarterly_data.signal: Management reaffirmed 0% to 4% full-year 2026 revenue growth on a comparable continuing-operations basis and expects software revenue at or above the high end and services at or below the low end of that range, with the first-half pattern of software outperforming services continuing into Q3 and Q4. The adjusted EBITDA margin guide of 29% to 31% compares with the 30% to 32% range given in May; management attributes the change to the divestiture, not the remaining business's performance. Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin was 28.1% and margins are expected to improve through the second half as savings are realized. Full-year adjusted diluted EPS from continuing operations is now expected at $0.31 to $0.36, with 155 million to 157 million fully diluted shares and an effective tax rate of approximately 30%.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue growth 0% to 4%; adjusted EBITDA margin 29% to 31% (was 30% to 32%); Q2 margin 28.1%; adjusted diluted EPS $0.31 to $0.36; 155 million to 157 million shares

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jon Resnick: regulators are accelerating model-informed approaches into policy. In the quarter HHS launched Operation TrialBlazer to speed up early-stage clinical trials and the FDA issued new guidance backing quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) modeling for first-in-human dosing; in July ICH M15 took effect at EMA, giving the U.S. and Europe a shared standard for model-informed drug development for the first time. Certara scientists produced 62 peer-reviewed publications in the quarter. He sees no customer hesitancy from the evolving guidance: there is a time lag before widespread adoption, but demand and questions are increasing.

CEO Jon Resnick: Certara's clinical pharmacology and pharmacometrics teams partnered with a biopharma company on the evidence package behind the FDA's approval of a new therapy for a rare autoimmune condition. In oncology, Certara scientists partnered with Memorial Sloan Kettering to build a virtual patient model on a Certara platform for CAR-T therapy in multiple myeloma, to individualize treatment and optimize trials of novel combination therapies.
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: research partner (CAR-T virtual patient model in multiple myeloma)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Jon Resnick: in the quarter Certara won its first major Simcyp deal in China and expanded engagement across the Middle East; in Japan a full modeling collaboration delivered a first-in-human dose estimate through CertaraIQ, its AI-powered QSP platform. He said China, Japan and the Middle East are not huge contributors today but offer outsized growth potential, and teams were built there over the last few months.

contracts.signal: CEO Jon Resnick: one of the quarter's 13 FDA novel approvals was Eli Lilly's orforglipron, the first once-daily non-peptide oral GLP-1 therapy for obesity; Certara's Simcyp Simulator supported the drug-to-drug interaction labeling and helped characterize how slower gastric emptying affects dosing. The product was approved in just 50 days, the fastest new molecular entity approval since 2002.
